angle: LoCoMo results claimed by memory systems, 2025-2026: what each number measures (reader, judge, category subset, denominator), how the vendor disputes played out, dataset-quality audits, category-ID mislabeling (checked with arithmetic against category sizes and released per-question files), the official LoCoMo repo license, and the original paper's metrics. Light compute only: I read a few small run-artifact JSONs (under 1.1 MB each) through the GitHub API. No datasets were downloaded and no tests were run.

items.metric: Dataset license, released size, and category-ID mapping implied by the official eval code
items.value: License is CC BY-NC 4.0 (LICENSE.txt: 'Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International'). locomo10.json is a 10-conversation subset: 1,986 QA = cat1 282, cat2 321, cat3 96, cat4 841, cat5 446. Code mapping: 1=multi-hop, 2=temporal, 3=open-domain, 4=single-hop, 5=adversarial. task_eval/evaluation_stats.py prints categories in the order keys=[4,1,2,3,5] to match the paper's table order (single, multi, temporal, open, adversarial). Category ID-to-name mapping is not documented in the README (issue #29).
items.denominator_exclusions: 1,986 total; the standard 'answerable' set is 1,540 (cats 1-4). MemR3 reports 12 duplicated questions, which gives 830 single-hop / 445 adversarial after dedup; Memori uses 1,529.
items.notes: Checked directly in the repo tree via gh api. Cat-5 items carry 'adversarial_answer' instead of 'answer', which is why most systems drop them. Open issues: #27 (label errors), #35 (conv-26 ground-truth errors), #42 (conv-41 typo), #43 (two cat-5 questions answerable from the transcript), #30 (duplicated condition bug in gpt_utils.py). The paper describes 50 conversations / 7,512 QA (Table 5); only 10 are released. I could not verify whether the paper's QA tables were computed on the 50 or the 10.

items.system: LoCoMo paper (Maharana et al., ACL 2024, arXiv 2402.17753)
items.metric: QA F1: SQuAD-style token F1 after normalization plus Porter stemming. Cat 1 (multi-hop) splits the gold answer on commas and averages the max partial F1. Cat 5 scores 1 if the output contains 'no information available' or 'not mentioned'.
items.value: Overall F1 incl. adversarial: human 87.9 (single 95.1 / multi 85.8 / temporal 92.6 / open 75.4 / adv 89.4); GPT-4-turbo (4K) 32.1; GPT-3.5-turbo 22.4; GPT-3.5-turbo-16K full 16K context 37.8; Mistral-7B 13.9; Llama-2-Chat-70B 17.9. Best RAG (GPT-3.5-turbo-16K, observations, top-5) 41.4 F1.
items.denominator_exclusions: Adversarial included in the overall. Whether the 10- or 50-conversation set was used is not stated.
items.notes: F1 code checked in task_eval/evaluation.py (f1_score uses PorterStemmer). The original paper used F1; LLM-judge 'J' was introduced later by Mem0 and is not the original metric.

items.system: LoCoMo paper RAG retrieval recall (GPT-3.5-turbo-16K reader)
items.metric: Retrieval recall@k (Table 3). Official code: per question, the fraction of gold evidence dialog IDs found in the retrieved context (partial recall, averaged). For session-summary retrieval, an evidence item counts as hit if its session is retrieved. Questions with empty evidence get recall = 1.
items.value: Overall recall (incl. adversarial). Dialog: k=5 58.8, k=10 67.5, k=25 79.9, k=50 84.8. Observation: k=5 49.6, k=10 57.1, k=25 66.0, k=50 71.1. Session summary: k=2 61.5, k=5 75.1, k=10 90.7. Matching overall F1, dialog: 31.7/34.6/35.8/34.8; observation: 41.4/38.8/38.0/37.8; summary: 29.9/32.5/31.5. Per-category dialog k=50 recall: single 90.4, multi 75.5, temporal 97.3, open 67.9, adv 77.7.
items.budget: top-k units = dialog turns, observations, or session summaries
items.notes: This is fractional evidence recall, neither recall_any nor recall_all. Empty-evidence questions count as perfect recall, which inflates the score. Code: https://github.com/snap-research/locomo/blob/main/task_eval/evaluation.py

items.metric: Gold-answer error audit of the 1,540 cat 1-4 questions, plus a judge-leniency stress test
items.value: 99/1,540 (6.4%) score-corrupting gold errors, so the theoretical ceiling is 93.57%. Errors by type: hallucination 33, temporal 26, speaker attribution 24, ambiguous 13, incomplete 3. Per-category error rate and ceiling: cat1 multi-hop 28/282 (ceiling 90.1%), cat2 temporal 26/321 (91.9%), cat3 open-domain 9/96 (90.6%), cat4 single-hop 36/841 (95.7%). A further 57 citation-only evidence errors (3.7%) and 4 structurally invalid evidence IDs. Judge leniency: gpt-4o-mini with published judge prompts accepted 62.81% of intentionally wrong 'vague but on-topic' answers and 10.61% of 'specific but wrong' answers.
items.judge: gpt-4o-mini with the EverMemOS eval-pipeline prompts (evaluation/config/prompts.yaml)
items.denominator_exclusions: 1,540 (cat 5 excluded); separately notes 446 cat-5 questions are never evaluated
items.notes: Third-party audit, not by the LoCoMo authors. Also reports: a GPT-4.1-mini full-context CoT answer prompt scores 92.62%, above EverMemOS's 92.32% and its claimed full-context 91.21%; EverMemOS's claimed 2,298 average tokens is 6,669 when measured; Wilson 95% CIs make 56% of adjacent comparisons indistinguishable. Write-up (April 8, 2026): https://penfieldlabs.substack.com/p/we-audited-locomo-64-of-the-answer. The audit's category mapping (1=multi, 2=temporal, 3=open, 4=single) matches the official code.

items.system: Mem0 (paper, arXiv 2504.19413, Chhikara et al., April 28 2025)
items.metric: LLM-as-a-Judge 'J' accuracy: binary CORRECT/WRONG, mean ± SD over 10 runs, micro-average over the 1,540 cat 1-4 questions
items.value: Mem0 66.88 ± 0.15; Mem0g (graph) 68.44 ± 0.17; full-context 72.90 ± 0.19; Zep (as run by Mem0) 65.99; LangMem 58.10; OpenAI memory 52.90; A-Mem 48.38; best RAG (k=2, 256-token chunks) 60.97. Per category as labeled in the paper, Mem0: single 67.13 / multi 51.15 / open 72.93 / temporal 55.51.
items.judge: gpt-4o-mini, temperature 0. Prompt says to 'be generous with your grading - as long as it touches on the same topic as the gold answer, it should be counted as CORRECT'
items.budget: Mem0 retrieves s=10 memories; embeddings text-embedding-3-small. 'Memory tokens' (~7k Mem0, ~14k Mem0g, 26,031 full-context) is total stored memory per conversation, not per-query context.
items.denominator_exclusions: Cat 5 skipped in code (evals.py: 'Skip category 5'). Paper says ~200 Qs/conversation; code gives 1,540.
items.code_license: mem0 repo Apache-2.0. The in-repo evaluation/ folder was retired on 2026-06-13 (commit 9315e30) in favor of mem0ai/memory-benchmarks.
items.artifacts: No per-question outputs for the paper runs found.
items.notes: Category labels are rotated relative to the official mapping (my arithmetic, verified): the paper's 'single-hop' = cat1 (282, really multi-hop), 'multi-hop' = cat3 (96, really open-domain), 'open-domain' = cat4 (841, really single-hop), 'temporal' = cat2. Size-weighting the paper's per-category J under this mapping reproduces the stated overalls exactly (66.88 Mem0, 68.44 Mem0g, 65.99 Zep); the literal labels give 62.14 for Mem0. The LoCoMo/ReadAgent/MemoryBank/MemGPT baseline rows were copied from A-Mem v1 and relabeled. The same misalignment is flagged by MemR3 (arXiv 2512.20237, section 4.4).

items.system: Mem0 new algorithm ('v3', April 2026) via mem0ai/memory-benchmarks
items.metric: Binary LLM-judge accuracy on 1,540 cat 1-4 questions
items.value: README (updated 2026-05-13): 92.5% (1425/1540) at top-200, 91.8% (1414/1540) at top-50; mem0.ai/research says 92.5 at 6,956 mean tokens. The April launch figure was 91.6. The committed per-question artifacts, which I recomputed, give 91.56% (1410/1540) at top-200 (cat1 263/282, cat2 298/321, cat3 73/96, cat4 776/841) and 82.66% (1273/1540) at top-50. These do not match the README's 92.5/91.8.
items.reader: gpt-5 (Azure) according to artifact metadata; the README's stated default is gpt-4o
items.judge: gpt-5 (Azure) according to artifact metadata. New judge template (benchmarks/locomo/prompts.py) is far more lenient: 'at least one correct item' counts as CORRECT; dates within 14 days and durations within 50% are CORRECT; a 'same referent' rule; an optional evidence rule that accepts answers diverging from gold.
items.cost_latency: From the artifact, search latency p50 3,056 ms / p95 6,009 ms at top-200; p50 916 ms / p95 1,211 ms at top-50
items.denominator_exclusions: Cats 1-4 (CATEGORIES_TO_EVALUATE=[1,2,3,4]); uses the correct code mapping (1 multi, 2 temporal, 3 open, 4 single)
items.artifacts: Yes: results/platform/locomo_results.json and locomo_top50_results.json. Metadata shows 156 (top-200) and 274 (top-50) questions 'merged_from_questions', meaning reruns were merged into the final file.
items.notes: The 2026-05-13 commit that raised the README to 92.5 changed only README.md, with no new artifacts. Example of judge leniency from the file: conv0_q0 gold '7 May 2023'; the generated answer listed 'May 7, 2023' and 'June 26, 2023' and was judged CORRECT. The reproduction complaint in mem0 issue #3944 (LLM score ~0.20 on the Mem0 platform, dates stored as January 2026 instead of dataset timestamps) was closed without a visible fix.

items.system: Zep (2025 rebuttal: 'Lies, Damn Lies, & Statistics', May 6 2025)
items.metric: Binary LLM-judge accuracy on 1,540 cat 1-4 questions, using the Mem0 'generous' judge prompt
items.value: 75.14 ± 0.17 (README). Recomputing the committed grades file gives 1157/1540 = 75.13% (single run). README per-category: single 79.79, multi 74.11, open 66.04, temporal 67.71. Search p95 0.632 s with concurrent searches.
items.notes: My recomputation from zep_locomo_grades.json: cat1 209/282 = 74.11, cat2 212/321 = 66.04, cat3 65/96 = 67.71, cat4 671/841 = 79.79. So the README calls cat2 (temporal) 'open domain' and cat3 (open-domain) 'temporal', a 2-to-3 swap. The blog originally claimed ~84%. Mem0 CTO (zep-papers issue #5, closed May 19 2025) said cat-5 correct answers were counted in the numerator while the denominator excluded them (+25.56 pp), and reported Zep at 58.44 ± 0.20 under Mem0's prompt and 10 runs. Zep corrected to 75.14 and in turn says Mem0 misconfigured Zep (both speakers as one user, timestamps in text, sequential search). Blog: https://blog.getzep.com/lies-damn-lies-statistics-is-mem0-really-sota-in-agent-memory/

Honest rows from the project's BENCHMARKS.md, all top-10 on 1,986 questions including adversarial: session, no rerank R@10 60.3%; dialog R@10 48.0%; hybrid v5 R@5 83.7% / R@10 88.9%; bge-large + Haiku rerank (top-15) R@10 96.3%.
items.budget: top_k=50 is more than every conversation's 19-32 sessions, so the whole conversation is always retrieved

The project's own note says the retrieval stage returns every session by construction, so the number measures an LLM's reading comprehension. The audit is issue #29 (https://github.com/milla-jovovich/mempalace/issues/29). Related LongMemEval '100%' was recall_any@5, retrieval only, with three hand-patched questions and Haiku rerank; held-out figure 98.4% R@5 on 450 questions; raw 96.6% R@5 is ChromaDB default embeddings. Issue #875 says the README and website still mix retrieval recall with competitors' QA accuracy.

items.metric: Rescored accuracy with a cleaned dataset and a stricter judge
items.value: 337 samples revised; 1,382 questions. Stricter judge (Qwen3-14B) has 86.33% agreement with human labels vs 43.67% for the original judge setup. Rescored: MemoraX 82.65, MemOS 63.60 (-17.30), MemPalace 58.68 (-15.78), EverMemOS 58.25 (-22.07), Mem0 48.91 (-15.56).
items.notes: Third-party. I did not verify the exact denominator derivation or the reader models.

items.metric: 'Memory accuracy' and 'adversarial robustness' (refusal on facts never disclosed)
items.value: 94.4% memory accuracy; 99.6% adversarial robustness
items.benchmark: LoCoMo, stated as 10 conversations and 1,813 questions
items.notes: The 1,813 denominator matches neither 1,540 nor 1,986. One of the few papers that scores cat 5. Reader and judge not verified.

items.metric: Evaluation-protocol audit
items.value: Flags a category-index ambiguity that caused misalignment in Mem0 (Chhikara et al. 2025) and MIRIX (Wang & Chen 2025). Correct counts: multi 282, temporal 321, open 96, single 830 (after dedup), adversarial 445. Finds 12 duplicated questions.
items.notes: Corroborated by arXiv 2511.21726 (appendix E, Table E2: white-paper order vs code IDs) and by locomo issue #29.

key_takeaways: Most headline LoCoMo numbers are not directly comparable. The common protocol (Mem0 paper) scores 1,540 cat 1-4 questions with gpt-4o-mini as both reader and judge under a 'be generous' prompt. On that protocol: Mem0 66.88, Mem0g 68.44, full-context 72.90. Later claims change the reader (gemini-2.5-pro for Backboard 90.0, gpt-5 for Mem0 v3, gpt-5.4 for Zep 94.7, Gemini-3 for Hindsight 89.6) and the judge (GPT-4.1, GPT-OSS-120B, gpt-5, gpt-5.4). Continua found that swapping the reader alone adds ~10 pp.

Category IDs are mislabeled across papers, and I verified this with arithmetic. The official code mapping is 1=multi-hop (282), 2=temporal (321), 3=open-domain (96), 4=single-hop (841), 5=adversarial (446). The Mem0 paper uses 1=single, 2=temporal, 3=multi, 4=open: size-weighting its per-category J reproduces the published 66.88, 68.44 and 65.99 exactly, while the literal labels give 62.14. Memobase, Backboard (confirmed from its per-question files), Hindsight and Memanto inherit that rotation, so their 'multi-hop' is really the 96-question open-domain category. Zep's 2025 README swaps 2 and 3 (confirmed from its grades file). MIRIX's overall only reconciles with sequential labels (1=single, 2=multi, 3=open, 4=temporal). EverMemOS, MemMachine, MemOS-1031, Memori and Mem0's 2026 harness use the correct mapping. Overall scores are unaffected; per-category comparisons across papers are unreliable.

The data sets a ceiling. The locomo-audit found 99 of 1,540 gold answers (6.4%) score-corrupting (hallucination 33, temporal 26, attribution 24, ambiguous 13, incomplete 3), so the ceiling is ~93.57%. It also found 57 citation-only evidence errors and 4 invalid evidence IDs. gpt-4o-mini with the published prompts accepted 62.81% of deliberately vague-but-on-topic wrong answers. Claims of 94.4 to 94.7 therefore sit at or above the ceiling of the unaudited key.

Judges have become more lenient over time. Mem0's 2026 memory-benchmarks judge gives CORRECT for one matching item out of several, dates within 14 days, durations within 50%, and optionally accepts answers that diverge from gold when evidence supports them. Scores from this judge cannot be compared to the 2025 gpt-4o-mini 'generous' judge.

Released artifacts sometimes contradict headlines. Mem0's committed per-question files recompute to 91.56% (top-200) and 82.66% (top-50), with gpt-5 as reader and judge and 156 or 274 rerun questions merged in, while the README says 92.5% and 91.8% and was updated without new artifacts. Zep's 2026 page (94.7%, 1,459/1,540) has per-category counts that match no official category sizes and sum to 1,436 correct; I found no artifacts for it. Zep's 2025 grades recompute to 75.13%, and its December 2025 gpt-4o-mini runs to 80.32 ± 0.43 (10 runs, median retrieval 189 ms). Backboard's files recompute to exactly 1,386/1,540 = 90.0%.

Reproduction failures and disputes are on record. Zep's original ~84% counted cat-5 correct answers in the numerator but not the denominator; Mem0 reran Zep at 58.44 ± 0.20; Zep corrected to 75.14 and disputes Mem0's setup. EverMemOS issue #73 got 38.38% on conv-26 against a claimed 92-93%. Mem0 issue #3944 got ~0.20 because of a date-handling bug. On the stricter LoCoMo-Refined judge, EverMemOS drops to 58.25 and Mem0 to 48.91.

The '100% LoCoMo' claim (MemPalace) was session-level retrieval recall@10 with top_k=50, which exceeds every conversation's 19-32 sessions, plus Sonnet reranking. It was retracted on April 14, 2026. The honest figures are 60.3% R@10 raw and 88.9% hybrid on 1,986 questions including adversarial, and no QA was judged. Backboard's 99.95% came from training on the test conversations. Engram's 93.9% is turn-level R@5 on 1,982 questions, not QA.

Full context is a strong baseline. It scores 72.9 (Mem0 paper, gpt-4o-mini), 87.52 (MIRIX, gpt-4.1-mini), 80.6 (Nemori, gpt-4.1-mini) and 92.62 (audit, GPT-4.1-mini with a CoT prompt). Several systems, including MIRIX and LightMem on Qwen, score below it, and Nemori beats it by only 0.2-0.7 pp.

The original LoCoMo metrics are stemmed token F1 over all five categories (human 87.9, GPT-4-turbo 32.1, best RAG 41.4 with top-5 observations) and fractional evidence recall@k, where questions with no evidence count as recall 1 (dialog top-50 84.8, summary top-10 90.7). LLM-judge 'J' was added later by Mem0. The data license is CC BY-NC 4.0, and only 10 of the paper's 50 conversations are released.

Unverifiable or missing: no Cognee LoCoMo result exists; no 'Memento' system reports LoCoMo (Memanto does, at 87.1); memU's 92.09 and MemOS's 88.83 have no settings; Letta's 74.0 used a gpt-4.1 SimpleQA-style judge and has no per-question artifacts; SeCom's main LoCoMo table uses GPT-4-generated QA, not the official set.
